Also, the company concentrates transactions for food ingredients in its food and beverage division with specific suppliers. The company purchases processed foods, meat, vegetables and other items from Toho Food Service Co., Ltd., with purchases of ¥1,197 million in the fiscal year ended November 2025, equal to 46% of food ingredient purchases. entries.6cb9eb935dd232c4: The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the company mainly operates hotel facilities for accommodation and provides restaurant and other food and beverage services attached to them, and that it operates "HOTEL AZ" mainly in the Kyushu region. The business involves opening outlets along arterial roads (roadside) or near small and medium-sized stations, in areas with few other hotels, rather than near terminal stations or entertainment and dining districts, and offering systemized and standardized services at affordable prices to win the support of users. As of November 30, 2025, there were 91 HOTEL AZ outlets (88 company-operated and three franchised). Revenue for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥19,560 million (the previous fiscal year was ¥18,029 million). The company does not prepare consolidated financial statements, so all figures are those of the company on a non-consolidated basis.

entries.b1c229d4b8932fff: Operating profit for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥3,199 million (¥3,760 million in the previous fiscal year), ordinary profit was ¥2,842 million (¥3,405 million), and net income was ¥2,081 million (¥2,236 million), as revenue increased while profit decreased. The annual securities report states that although revenue increased, cost of sales rose to ¥2,607 million (¥2,298 million) due to soaring raw material prices, and selling, general and administrative expenses rose to ¥13,754 million (¥11,970 million) due to the costs of four new stores, higher personnel costs from raising salary levels, and increases in outsourcing fees, linen costs, utility costs and others. The company plans to fund capital expenditure for new stores mainly through borrowings from financial institutions; as of November 30, 2025, interest-bearing debt (including lease obligations) accounted for 38% of total assets.
